sources.section: Build your own Front-end Framework / Library
sources.entry: JavaScript: _A DIY guide to build your own React_

summary.one_liner: Didact is a step-by-step DIY guide, presented as a series of blog posts with matching code commits, for building a simplified React-like UI library from scratch.
summary.what_it_does: The repository accompanies a series of posts that build a React-style library incrementally. The README lists the stages: rendering DOM elements, element creation and JSX, the virtual DOM and reconciliation, components and state, Fiber-based incremental reconciliation, and Hooks. Each stage has a CodePen or CodeSandbox sample and git diffs showing the code changes. The README points readers to the final post as the self-contained version that includes everything. Posts are also available in Chinese.
use_cases: build a minimal virtual DOM library
follow a tutorial on React Fiber reconciliation
notable: Incremental tutorial with a git diff for each step of the build
Ends with a self-contained post covering Fiber and Hooks
Live code samples on CodePen and CodeSandbox
caveats: The README gives no install or run instructions; it is a guide, not a packaged library
Code is tied to the blog posts, so the repo is mainly for learning rather than production use
